original_problem.statement: Erman and Sam, Questions about Boij-Soderberg theory (arXiv:1606.01867), Question 6.1: is every integral point of every pure ray in three variables the Betti table of a finite length module over k[x,y,z] or over the enveloping algebra U(H) of the Heisenberg Lie algebra? Question 6.2 is its analogue in four variables.
original_problem.priority: Jiang, Li, Sun, Wang, Xiao and Yu (arXiv:2605.25259, Theorems 3.7 and 3.8) answer both questions negatively over every field, with (1,2,9,8) on (0,6,20,21) and (1,2,5,6,2) on (0,1,4,5,6). Boocher, Huang and Wolf (arXiv:2512.24320) hold the polynomial-ring half of both examples and the classification of the rays with two generators. The pure modules over U(H) from Kostant's theorem are stated by Erman and Sam and announced by Sam. The obstructions over k[x,y,z] used here are those of Buchsbaum and Eisenbud, Erman, and Boij and Soderberg.
original_problem.prohibited_reframing: No CAOS result may be described as the first negative answer to Question 6.1 or 6.2, as a new obstruction over k[x,y,z], or as a result on the Kostant family. A realization found by a search over a prime field is a statement over that field until it is recomputed over the rationals.

mission: Decide, for the pure rays (0,d1,d2,d3) of small degree, which primitive points are Betti tables of finite length modules over k[x,y,z] and over U(H), with explicit modules and exact computations: the least d3 of a counterexample to Question 6.1, the least realizable multiple on each ray, and how the answers depend on the characteristic of the field.

focuses.title: The realizability table for d3 <= 12 and the least counterexample to Question 6.1
focuses.target: For the 220 pure rays with d3 <= 12: the primitive point realized, excluded or open over k[x,y,z], with the least realizable multiple; the parity-passing excluded rays over U(H); hence the least d3 of a counterexample in characteristic 0.
focuses.value: The published counterexample has d3 = 21; the table shows where the question first fails and separates the two rings. The family U/U(x^e, y^e) and the characteristic 2 statement came out of it.
focuses.success_gate: Every ray with d3 <= 9 decided in characteristic 0 by an explicit module, a cited construction or a cited obstruction, each hit recomputed in a second system (met 2026-11-19: EXP-001, EXP-002, EXP-003).
stop_conditions: A hit on a point excluded by a published obstruction (a bug or a refuted proof): stop and explain.
The search budget of EXP-001 is reached with rays with d3 <= 9 still open.
focuses.novelty_status: Not found in the searches of 2026-11-19 (the literature pass and the two reviews): the modules U/U(x^e, y^e), the dependence of Question 6.1 on the characteristic, a statement of the least d3 of a counterexample. The two rays with d3 = 10 were identified in the programme's dossier of 2026-09-02 from published obstructions. A negative search is not a proof of novelty.

focuses.title: First manuscript: pure resolutions over U(H), the characteristic, and the census
focuses.target: One manuscript with: the family U/U(x^e, y^e) and its sharp characteristic condition with full proofs; the characteristic 2 statement on (0,2,6,8) with its proof; the table over U(H) of the parity-passing rays excluded over k[x,y,z] for d3 <= 12; the census over k[x,y,z] for d3 <= 12; the least d3 of a counterexample in characteristic 0; the methods (exact linear algebra over U(H), the census, the search and its rechecks), the limits and the open rays.
focuses.value: States a characteristic-dependent answer to Question 6.1 on a point that passes the known numerical test, an infinite family of pure modules over U(H) outside the Kostant family, and counterexamples with d3 = 10 against the published d3 = 21, with reproducible exact evidence.
focuses.success_gate: A manuscript at the content bar, every statement traced to a proof or an artifact, read by a reviewer other than the writer with no blocker left, and published on Zenodo with its record metadata (met 2026-11-20: v0.01, 10.5281/zenodo.24385387).
stop_conditions: The review of the least-counterexample statement finds a failing case: the statement is narrowed to what holds before any text claims it.
A source is found that already contains the family, the characteristic dependence or the least counterexample: the manuscript cites it and keeps only what remains.
Two review rounds leave a blocker open: stop and bring the blocker to the next strategic review.
focuses.novelty_status: As in BSR-F1; the manuscript states the searches made and claims no priority.
focuses.first_bounded_action: Done: the reviews of the three derivations and of the lift lemma, the writing, the review with its fix passes and the release. Next: the strategic review that names the following focus (BSR-F3 is proposed).
focuses.review_2026_11_20: Success gate met on 2026-11-20 (v0.01 published, 10.5281/zenodo.24385387). Strategic review of the same day, made under the standing instruction to choose and advance the case with the best prospects: the focus closes and BSR-F3 becomes current.

focuses.title: The characteristic questions left open by the first manuscript, and the open rays
focuses.target: (1) The machine checks of the characteristic 2 theorem and of the family at e = 6, 7 archived with the repository's instrument (EXP-005). (2) The point (1,2,2,1) on (0, e, 3e, 4e) in odd characteristic below 2e, for e = 3 and 4: a pure pair of forms over GF(p), or a recorded negative with its method (EXP-006). (3) The 15 rays with d3 >= 10 whose primitive point is open over k[x,y,z]. (4) The substitution of x^e, y^e in the Kostant presentations.
focuses.value: Item (2) decides whether characteristic 2 is the only characteristic in which the point fails for small e, and whether the family U/U(x^e, y^e) is part of a larger family of pure modules (the locus of the rank condition has dimension at least 12 in a Grassmannian of dimension 14 at e = 4, by a Thom-Porteous class computed before the run). Item (1) gives the manuscript an artifact for each machine claim.
focuses.success_gate: EXP-005 confirmed with its four gates; for e = 3 and e = 4 and every odd prime below 2e, either a pure pair confirmed in a second system or a recorded negative with its method; the outcome reviewed by a reader other than the writer before the manuscript states it (v0.02).
stop_conditions: A finite length module with at most one more relation than generators in characteristic 2 (a defect or a refuted proof): stop and examine before anything else.
Three consecutive experiments decide no characteristic question and no ray.
A source is found that already contains the statement on odd characteristic: cite it and keep only what remains.
focuses.novelty_status: Open questions of this programme, stated in the limits section of the manuscript v0.01. Not searched as such beyond the literature pass of 2026-11-19; a search is due before any claim.
focuses.first_bounded_action: EXP-005 and EXP-006 CONFIRMED on 2026-11-20; the family-dimension derivation reviewed (correct after fixes). Next: BSB-025 (archive the review's tangent space computation and explicit pairs over QQ), then the manuscript v0.02 with its review.
focuses.review_2026_11_20: Items (1) and (2) of the target are met for e = 3 and 4: the point (1,2,2,1) of (0, e, 3e, 4e) is realized over U in every odd characteristic below 2e by explicit pairs (two instruments and a rebuild by the coordinating session); at e = 5 it is realized in characteristic 3 and open in 5 and 7. The success gate still needs the review of the verdicts by a reader other than the writer, with the manuscript v0.02.

manuscripts.split_action: No split: one central question (which primitive points of the pure rays of small degree are Betti tables of finite length modules over k[x,y,z] and over the Heisenberg enveloping algebra, and how the answer depends on the characteristic). v0.01 (2026-11-20) carries the family U/U(x^e, y^e) with its sharp characteristic condition, the general characteristic 2 theorem, the table over the enveloping algebra, the census over k[x,y,z] with the rank certificates and the lift proposition, and the least counterexample in characteristic 0 (EXP-001 to EXP-004). A new version for corrections, for a decided open ray or for a decided characteristic question.
